title: Apply PID changes atomically and keep feedforward inside constraints
equipment: Variable-speed booster pump with recirculation valve
physicalPurpose: Change an online pressure-controller configuration without exposing mixed parameters and ensure every contribution passes through the same actuator constraints.
principalTechnique: Atomic PID configuration and constraint-aware signal ordering
objective: Apply a complete PID configuration as one revision and distinguish the valid internal feedforward path from an invalid post-limit sum.

simplifications: The unsafe sequential update is a simulation-only diagnostic and is not a supported configuration path.
The feedforward value is prescribed to expose signal ordering; disturbance modelling and feedforward design are deferred to Lesson 53.
The diagnostic nominal request mirrors this lesson's PI increment only and never participates in the plant-command path.

baseline.limitation: A sequential update exposes new proportional gain with old integral gain and produces a 15.1 percentage-point first increment that belongs to neither complete configuration.

change.decision: Assign the complete candidate record, call Configure once, and pass feedforward through PIDInput so the controller's anti-windup and output constraints remain authoritative.

disturbances: 20 percent prescribed feedforward contribution in the ordering comparison

acceptance.window: first 100 ms update with complete revision 1 and 1 bar setpoint step
first update after 20 percent feedforward from 40 percent applied output

abortPredicates: Any signal or candidate parameter is nonfinite
Pressure or applied valve command leaves its hard limit
A configuration record is incomplete or has not passed station-level validation
A command path can bypass controller and actuator constraints
safety.restorationMode: Station Disabled with 30 percent safe recirculation
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Never reproduce the mixed-revision or external post-limit sum on physical equipment; physical online changes require validated parameters, reviewed topology, rollback, and explicit approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Apply one coherent PID revision and verify that feedforward cannot bypass anti-windup or actuator constraints.
requiredVisibleEvidence: old, mixed, and new parameter records
active revision at the update scan

learning.context: The booster-pump pressure controller remains online while an engineer prepares a new PID configuration and while a measured disturbance may contribute feedforward output.
learning.reason: Lesson 28 aligned controller state between authority owners, but a scan can still be wrong if it mixes parameter revisions or adds a contribution after constraints have executed.
theory: A candidate configuration is the complete proposed PID record. The active configuration is the record used by the current controller scan. A revision identifies one complete record.
Atomic application exposes either the complete old record or complete new record to one update. A mixed record is invalid even if every individual value is numerically valid.
Feedback and feedforward combine inside Control.PID before anti-windup, amplitude limits, and rate limits. The rate interval begins at the previous applied output.
Requested and applied outputs are distinct engineering signals. A calculation added after the returned applied output bypasses controller state and limits and is rejected.
learning.workedPrediction: From 40 percent at 6 bar, new Kp 15 and Ki 3 produce a 15.3-point first increment for a 1 bar step; new Kp with old Ki produces 15.1. At zero error, 20 percent feedforward with a 20 percent-per-second limit over 0.1 seconds permits 42 percent from the previous 40, while a rejected post-limit sum is 60 percent.
practicalPreparation: Verify SP, PV, actual and applied valve values, candidate and active parameters, revision, configured-this-scan, feedforward, rate bounds, limit flags, and simulation label.
Restore 6 bar and 40 percent. Keep plant, state, sample interval, limit, seed, and event timing equal across comparisons.
learning.baseline: Run the simulation-only sequential update for one scan so new proportional gain is combined with old integral gain, then reject the mixed revision.
learning.change: Restore, assign the complete candidate record and call Configure once before the controller update. Restore again and pass the prescribed feedforward through PIDInput rather than summing it after the returned output.
learning.comparison: Compare record coherence, first-update increment, applied-output rate, constraint state, and external-sum limit violation at exact scan boundaries.
learning.validation: Require every production update to expose a complete old or new record, reproduce 55.300 and 55.100 percent diagnostic outcomes, and apply 42.000 rather than the rejected 60.000 percent when the rate limit binds.
learning.explanation: Scan order and data ownership are part of the controller law. Atomic records prevent hybrid tuning, and one internal contribution path keeps state, anti-windup, and physical limits consistent.
learning.transfer: Use the same snapshot and ordering rule for online tuning, scheduling, selectors, and multiloop control. Lesson 30 next defines deterministic behavior when configuration, signal, or timing data are invalid.
